people.name: Edward Theodore Gein
people.role: Plainfield, Wisconsin farmer and handyman (1906-1984); the only person charged in Worden's killing

history.detail: Arrested that evening at a West Plainfield grocery store after the antifreeze sales slip pointed to him (C22, C23).
Taken to the State Crime Lab, Madison, for lie-detector and other tests (17 and 19 Nov) (C29).
Crime-lab director's Madison statement: Gein admitted killing Mrs. Worden 'last Saturday' (C30).
Charged in Waushara County with first-degree murder of Worden (one count); pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity (C40). Arraignment date 21 Nov 1957 single weak source.
Sent to Central State Hospital, Waupun, for 30 days' observation (C41).
Found incompetent to stand trial; committed to Central State Hospital by Judge Herbert A. Bunde (C41). Alt. dates 16 Jan / Mar 1958.
Found competent to stand trial (C43).
Confession reportedly excluded by Judge Gollmar (Schley assault, Miranda) - UNVERIFIED, single weak source (C46).
Bench trial before Judge Robert H. Gollmar, no jury (C43).

Found guilty of first-degree murder, then found legally insane at the time; committed to a state mental hospital, not prison. Some sources call the outcome 'not guilty by reason of insanity'; UPI 1984 said 'never convicted' (C44, C45).
Petitioned for release; denied after evaluations (C48).
Moved from Central State Hospital to Mendota Mental Health Institute, Madison; year conflicts (C49).
Died at Mendota, aged 77; respiratory failure, also had cancer (C50).

matters.notes: Status CONVICTED is shorthand: the 1968 court found he committed first-degree murder but was legally insane, so he was committed indefinitely and never imprisoned. On-screen wording: 'Found guilty of murder - and legally insane'. Never write 'convicted' without the insanity finding.

history.detail: Admitted killing Hogan in December 1954, per the crime-lab director's statement; her remains identified at the farm (C15).
Not tried; only Worden's killing was tried (C16). Reason ('prohibitive costs') single weak source (C17).

matters.notes: Admitted, never charged or tried; no court finding. Say 'he admitted killing Mary Hogan', never 'convicted of'.

history.detail: Reported Henry missing after a brush fire; accounts say he led searchers to the body (C07).
State investigator Joe Wilimovsky reportedly raised Henry's death during questioning - single source (C11).

matters.notes: Never accused by any authority; death officially recorded as accidental asphyxiation; no autopsy. Later suspicion is writers' speculation only (C08-C10).

history.detail: Admitted robbing graves; test exhumations matched his account (C32).

matters.notes: No charge for grave robbing was found in the research. Count of graves disputed (C33).

history.detail: 1957 statement on behalf of five DAs cleared him of three well-known disappearance cases; passed a polygraph in at least the Hartley case (C36).

matters.notes: No evidence ever tied him to any other killing (C34, C36). Do not name these cases (C37).

people.name: Bernice Worden
people.role: Plainfield hardware store owner, 58; killed 16 Nov 1957

history.detail: Disappeared from her store in the morning; her body was found that night in a shed on the Gein farm; she had been shot (C19, C24).

matters.notes: Narrate who she was and what was taken from her town; nothing about the condition of her body (C25). 'Widow' NOT confirmed (Q34). Age 58 single reference source.

people.name: Mary Hogan
people.role: Tavern operator, Pine Grove, Wisconsin; disappeared 8 Dec 1954

history.detail: Last seen at her tavern; blood and a spent cartridge found; case went cold (C14).
Remains identified at the Gein farm; Gein admitted killing her (C15).

matters.notes: Age reported as 51 or 54 - do not state (C14). Buried in Plainfield Cemetery (C52). No court ever ruled on her death.

people.name: Henry George Gein
people.role: Ed Gein's older brother; died aged 43 in 1944

history.detail: Died during a brush fire on/near the family farm (C06).
Coroner listed asphyxiation; police dismissed foul play; no autopsy or investigation (C08).
Biographer Harold Schechter reported bruises on his head; others call the death suspicious (C09, C10).

matters.notes: No finding of homicide; no one ever charged. Netflix's depiction of Ed killing him is invented (C70). Status: death on the record as accidental; later doubts are speculation.

people.name: Augusta Wilhelmine Gein
people.role: Ed's mother; died 29 Dec 1945 aged 67

history.detail: Died after a second stroke (C12).

matters.notes: Characterised by biographers as domineering and religious (C02). Not accused of anything; avoid making her the 'cause'. Her rooms were sealed after her death (C13).

people.name: George Philip Gein
people.role: Ed's father

history.detail: Death in 1940 per one source (C02).

matters.notes: Described as an alcoholic (C02). Buried in Plainfield Cemetery (C52). Middle name 'Philip' is general knowledge NOT in this research - verify or drop.

people.name: Frank Worden
people.role: Bernice Worden's son; Waushara County deputy sheriff

history.detail: Entered his mother's store about 5 p.m., found register open and blood; told investigators Gein was to return for antifreeze; the sales slip led to Gein (C21, C22).

matters.notes: Also a victim's family member. Speculation that he was involved in the 1958 fire or bought the land is unsupported - never use (C56, C57).

people.name: Arthur Schley
people.role: Waushara County sheriff, 1957

history.detail: Led the search of the Gein farm; found Worden's body in a shed (C24).
Reportedly assaulted Gein during interrogation; said to have led to the confession's exclusion - UNVERIFIED (C46).
Died aged 43, before the trial; never testified (C47).

matters.notes: Allegation of assault rests on Crime+Investigation plus a weak blog. A tie-in blog asks whether he burned the farmhouse - pure speculation, never use (C56).

people.name: Robert H. Gollmar
people.role: Circuit judge who presided over the 1968 trial; author of Edward Gein: America's Most Bizarre Murderer (1981)

history.detail: Bench trial; found Gein committed first-degree murder and was legally insane (C43, C44).
Published book on the case (C74).

matters.notes: His book is the key unread source.

people.name: Herbert A. Bunde
people.role: Judge who committed Gein as incompetent, 1958

history.detail: Committed Gein to Central State Hospital after psychiatrists testified he was not competent (C41).

matters.notes: Single 1968-era newspaper passage.

people.name: Earl Kileen
people.role: Waushara County District Attorney (named in a 2025 timeline)

history.detail: Report reportedly called the scene 'a museum of psychosis' - UNVERIFIED (C28).

matters.notes: Role in the charging decision not confirmed (Q26). Spelling unverified.

people.name: Joe Wilimovsky
people.role: Wisconsin state investigator

history.detail: Reportedly questioned Gein and raised Henry's death - single source (C11).

matters.notes: Unverified.

people.name: Wisconsin State Crime Laboratory director ("Wilson")
people.role: Issued the Madison statement on Gein's admissions, Nov 1957

history.detail: Statement on behalf of five DAs: Gein admitted killing Worden and Hogan; cleared of three disappearance cases (C15, C30, C36).

matters.notes: Only the surname 'Wilson' appears in the quoted text. Full name not confirmed - do not expand.

people.name: Adeline Watkins
people.role: Plainfield resident described in 1957 press as Gein's sweetheart

history.detail: Minneapolis Tribune interview (reprinted in Wisconsin State Journal) described a 20-year romance (C63).
Within days said the account was exaggerated; admitted only a few outings (C63).

matters.notes: Private individual; not a witness to any crime. Netflix built a romance plot she denied. Use only to illustrate press myth-making.

people.name: Harold Schechter
people.role: Biographer; author of Deviant: The Shocking True Story of Ed Gein, the Original 'Psycho' (reissued 1 April 2025)

history.detail: Reported bruises on Henry's head (C09).

matters.notes: Key secondary source; book not read.

history.detail: Called the series' opening autoerotic-asphyxiation scene fiction (C70).

people.name: George Arndt
people.role: Writer who studied the case

history.detail: Wrote that it was 'possible and likely' Henry's death was 'the Cain and Abel aspect of this case' (C10).

matters.notes: Opinion; attribute.

people.name: Bunny Gibbons
people.role: Illinois carnival sideshow promoter

history.detail: Bought the 1949 Ford for $760 (C58).
Exhibited it as the 'Ed Gein Ghoul Car' until objections shut it down (C58).

people.name: Enden Schey
people.role: Wisconsin real-estate broker named in a 1958 photo caption as highest bidder for the farm

history.detail: Highest bidder; planned to plant the 195 acres in pine (C57).

matters.notes: Name from one archive caption; spelling unverified.

people.name: Robert Bloch
people.role: Author of the novel Psycho (1959)

history.detail: Psycho, inspired by the case; said he based it 'on the situation, rather than on any person' (C64).

people.name: Tobe Hooper
people.role: Director, The Texas Chain Saw Massacre (1974)

history.detail: Confirmed Gein was one of his inspirations (C65).

people.name: John Douglas
people.role: Retired FBI profiler

history.detail: Said Buffalo Bill was 'a composite of three killers' (C66).

matters.notes: Thomas Harris has never officially named his sources.

people.name: Charlie Hunnam
people.role: Actor; played Gein in Monster: The Ed Gein Story

history.detail: Series released (C67).
First Emmy nomination, lead actor; also Golden Globe nominee; did not win the Emmy (C71).

people.name: Ian Brennan
people.role: Co-creator/showrunner of Monster: The Ed Gein Story

history.detail: 'Ed at its core is a story of mental illness.' (C69)
